items.label: fig:diffusion_geometry_framework
items.caption_tex: Overview of diffusion-geometric reconstruction of cosmological vector fields. The upper branch shows global field representation and regularization, while the lower branch shows the local differential structure and metric calibration. Nystr\"om extension and the three distinct levels of weighting are also indicated.

items.label: fig:mock1_diffusion_modes_spectrum
items.caption_tex: Diffusion eigenfunctions and the normalized generator spectrum constructed from the complete Mock-1 sample. (a)--(c) The first, eighth, and thirty-second nonconstant modes, displayed on the slab $|z|\leq12.5\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ around the center of the sphere. Each point represents a galaxy position. For each mode, the displayed values are normalized by the 99th percentile of $|\phi_a|$ within the slab and clipped to $[-1,1]$. Because the sign of an eigenfunction is arbitrary, it is fixed so that $\phi_a>0$ at the point with the largest absolute value. (d) Normalized generator weights $\widetilde{\eta}_a$ for the 2047 nonconstant modes contained in the 2048-mode geometry. We define $\widetilde{\eta}_a=\eta_a/\operatorname{median}_{1\leq b\leq511}\eta_b$. The circles mark $a=1,8,32$, corresponding to panels (a)--(c).

items.label: fig:gradient_calibration_conditioning
items.caption_tex: Numerical diagnostics of the metric-calibrated gradient on the complete Mock-1 sample. (a) Comparison of the RMS vector errors of the raw coordinate covector and metric-calibrated gradient for the coordinate functions $x$, $y$, and $z$. The vertical axis is logarithmic. (b) Distribution of the condition number $\kappa_i$ of the local Gram matrix over all $10000$ points. The solid, dashed, and dotted lines indicate the median, 90th percentile, and 99th percentile, respectively. The inset in the upper right gives the maximum condition number and the fraction of points at which the eigenvalue cutoff was applied.

items.label: fig:mock1_scale_dependence
items.caption_tex: Reconstruction performance at the validation-selected practical truncation in Mock-1. (a) Test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ of the diffusion-spectral estimator and adaptive local-kernel baseline. (b) Median velocity-direction error of the same two methods. (c) Calibration slopes of the Cartesian components $v_x$, $v_y$, and $v_z$ for the diffusion-spectral estimator. The dashed line indicates unity. Points and error bars in panels (a)--(c) show the mean and $1$ standard deviation over five replicates. (d) Paired test difference $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D,\mathrm{diff}}-\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D,\mathrm{local}}$ in each replicate. Small points show individual replicates, while diamonds and error bars show the mean and $1$ standard deviation. The reference smoothing scale and adopted $n_{\mathrm b}$ are indicated on the horizontal axis.

items.label: fig:mock1_mode_number_convergence
items.caption_tex: Dependence on retained mode number in Mock-1. For each of the fine, fiducial, and coarse reference fields, points and error bars show the mean and $1$ standard deviation over the five reference-model splits. (a) $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ on the held-out test set. (b) Median velocity-direction error. (c) Through-origin vector gain $g_{\mathrm v}$. The dashed line indicates unity. (d) Paired test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ difference relative to $n_{\mathrm b}=1024$. Negative values indicate lower test error than the 1024-mode estimator. Connecting lines are guides to the eye.

items.label: fig:mock2_mode_number_convergence
items.caption_tex: Convergence with retained mode number in Mock-2. All panels use operator-side unweighted geometry, and the regularization strength is selected from the parent-weighted validation risk for each $n_{\mathrm b}$ and loss model. (a) Parent-weighted validation $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. (b) Parent-weighted observed-test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. (c) Primary complete-query $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. Points and error bars in panels (a)--(c) show the mean and $1$ standard deviation over ten label splits, and connecting lines are guides to the eye. (d) Paired difference between the selection-weighted and unweighted losses at the validation-selected practical truncation. Points show the ten-split mean, and error bars show the $95\%$ seed-bootstrap interval.

items.label: fig:mock2_weighting_capacity_interaction

items.label: fig:mock2_geometry_sensitivity
items.caption_tex: Restricted geometry sensitivity in Mock-2. All diffusion-spectral models use fixed $n_{\mathrm b}=2560$, and the regularization strength is selected from the parent-weighted validation risk in each split. (a) Parent-weighted observed-test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. (b) Observed-unweighted test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. (c) Primary complete-query $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. Points and error bars in panels (a)--(c) show the ten-split mean and $1$ standard deviation. (d) Parent-risk differences defined by subtracting the corresponding primary configuration from each alternative configuration. Points show the ten-split mean, and error bars show the $95\%$ seed-bootstrap interval. Positive values indicate higher risk for the alternative configuration named first.

items.label: fig:mock2_local_comparison
items.caption_tex: Same-split comparison of the diffusion-spectral estimator and adaptive local-kernel baseline in Mock-2. (a) Parent-weighted observed-test $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. (b) Primary complete-query $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$. Points and error bars in panels (a) and (b) show the ten-split mean and $1$ standard deviation. (c) Parent-risk contrasts. (d) Complete-query contrasts. All differences in panels (c) and (d) are defined as local minus diffusion. Points show the ten-split mean, and error bars show the $95\%$ seed-bootstrap interval. Positive values therefore indicate lower risk for the diffusion-spectral estimator. The first three comparisons use the primary unweighted diffusion estimator as the reference, while the final comparison uses the primary selection-weighted diffusion estimator.

items.label: fig:mock3_mode_number_convergence
items.caption_tex: Mode-number convergence of the primary unweighted estimator in Mock-3. Points and error bars in panels (a)--(c) show the mean and standard deviation across ten octant-stratified label splits. Panel (d) shows the error reduction between adjacent retained mode numbers, calculated from the split-averaged parent-weighted validation risk. (a) $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ on the parent-weighted validation and held-out observed samples. (b) $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ on the region-primary complete-query sample. (c) Dispersion of $\mathrm{NRMSE}_{3\mathrm D}$ among the eight octants for the observed and query samples. (d) Reduction in parent-weighted validation error between adjacent retained mode numbers. The dashed line indicates the $2\%$ practical threshold, and the dotted line indicates zero. Connecting lines are guides to the eye for visualizing mode-number dependence.

items.label: fig:mock1_practical_plateau_diagnostic
items.caption_tex: Practical-plateau diagnostic for Mock-1. The vertical axis shows the reduction in validation error relative to the preceding candidate mode number, as defined in Equation~\eqref{eq:adjacent_validation_reduction}. The dashed line indicates the $2\%$ practical threshold, and the dotted line indicates zero. Open diamonds mark the truncations jointly selected by Equations~\eqref{eq:practical_plateau_rule} and \eqref{eq:one_standard_error_mode_rule}. Negative values indicate an increase in validation error after adding modes. The smallest candidate, $n_{\mathrm b}=256$, has no diagnostic value because it has no preceding candidate for comparison.
